subject: Deriving density from CL model averaged values

messages.author: e8faec36caf7f7c7
messages.subject: Deriving density from CL model averaged values
parts:
Hi there,


I might have missed this information somewhere, but any thoughts would be appreciated.


I have fitted 5 conditional likelihood models, including one with an age covariate,  and compared via AICc. The dAICc values are close, so I'm hoping to model average the top models however I'm struggling to find a way to derive my density estimates from the model averaged values. I read on a 2012 forum that this used to be something you were unable to do in secr, so was just wondering if this issue has been cleared up? 


Thanks,

Charlotte Patterson

messages.author: edcd7a5fe9ad6473
messages.subject: Re: Deriving density from CL model averaged values
parts:
Hi Charlotte, if you have the delta aic values, you could in theory calculate the akaike weights, sensu Burnham and Anderson 2002, and then use those to calculate the density as a weighted average?
Mark

messages.author: edcd7a5fe9ad6473
messages.subject: Re: Deriving density from CL model averaged values
parts:
Hi Charlotte,
In theory, this approach is a general way to deal with model selection uncertainty, according to Burnham and Anderson, so it should apply in this case. You would take the 5 density estimates and calculate a weighted average, using the Akaike weights for each model as the weighing factors.

https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weighted_arithmetic_mean
